audits.title: Total mesorectal excision for rectal cancer--what can be achieved by a national audit?
audits.setting: National Norwegian Rectal Cancer Registry, all surgical departments

cycle1.result: Local recurrence 28%; 5-year overall survival 55% for under 75s.

audits.intervention: National TME training courses, pathologist training, a rectal cancer registry and regular feedback of departmental results.

cycle2.result: TME rose from 78% (1994) to 96% (1998); local recurrence 8% at 39 months; 5-year overall survival 71% for under 75s.

audits.citation: Wibe A, Eriksen MT, Syse A, Myrvold HE, Søreide O, Norwegian Rectal Cancer Group. Total mesorectal excision for rectal cancer--what can be achieved by a national audit?. Colorectal Dis. 2003;5(5):471-477. doi:10.1046/j.1463-1318.2003.00506.x. PMID: 12925083.

audits.title: Reduced Circumferential Resection Margin Involvement in Rectal Cancer Surgery: Results of the Dutch Surgical Colorectal Audit.
audits.standard: Reporting of circumferential resection margin (CRM) in pathology
audits.intervention: Introduction of national quality assurance audit (DSCA)
audits.other_findings: 12,669 patients in total; interhospital variation decreased and year of registration independently predicted CRM involvement.
audits.citation: Gietelink L, Wouters MW, Tanis PJ, Deken MM, Ten Berge MG, Tollenaar RA, et al.. Reduced Circumferential Resection Margin Involvement in Rectal Cancer Surgery: Results of the Dutch Surgical Colorectal Audit. J Natl Compr Canc Netw. 2015;13(9):1111-1119. doi:10.6004/jnccn.2015.0136. PMID: 26358795.

audits.title: Improving clinical outcomes through centralization of rectal cancer surgery and clinical audit: a mixed-methods assessment.
audits.standard: Clinical guidelines for rectal cancer care (quality indicators)
audits.setting: Hospitals performing rectal cancer surgery in Catalonia

cycle1.result: 51 hospitals performed rectal cancer surgery; 37.5% of patients operated in high-volume centres; total mesorectal excision reported 36.2; emergency surgery 5.6%; median lymph nodes examined 14.1.

audits.intervention: Centralisation of rectal cancer surgery to fewer hospitals.

cycle2.result: 32 hospitals; 52.8% in high-volume centres; total mesorectal excision reported 85.7; emergency surgery 3.6%; median lymph nodes 16.

audits.other_findings: Qualitative interviews (18) suggested a more integrated model of care is needed.
audits.citation: Prades J, Manchon-Walsh P, Solà J, Espinàs JA, Guarga A, Borras JM. Improving clinical outcomes through centralization of rectal cancer surgery and clinical audit: a mixed-methods assessment. Eur J Public Health. 2016;26(4):538-542. doi:10.1093/eurpub/ckv237. PMID: 26739995.

audits.title: Improving survival and local control in rectal cancer in Catalonia (Spain) in the context of centralisation: A full cycle audit assessment.
audits.standard: Regional clinical practice guideline quality indicators
audits.setting: All public hospitals performing radical rectal cancer surgery in Catalonia

cycle1.result: 84.0% of patients treated in centres with caseload over 11 per year; locoregional recurrence 4.5/100 person-years at two years.

audits.intervention: Centralisation of rectal cancer surgery to authorised centres, with ongoing clinical audit.

cycle2.result: 90.4% treated in higher-volume centres; locoregional recurrence 3.06/100 person-years (p = 0.005).

audits.other_findings: 3780 patients in total; mortality at three months, one and two years fell by 55%, 40% and 34%.
audits.citation: Manchon-Walsh P, Aliste L, Espinàs JA, Prades J, Guarga A, Balart J, et al.. Improving survival and local control in rectal cancer in Catalonia (Spain) in the context of centralisation: A full cycle audit assessment. Eur J Surg Oncol. 2016;42(12):1873-1880. doi:10.1016/j.ejso.2016.08.009. PMID: 27624916.

audits.title: Oncological adequacy of laparoscopic rectal cancer resection: An audit in Indian perspective.
audits.standard: Oncological quality measures: complete TME, CRM >=1 mm, negative distal margin, nodal harvest
audits.setting: Department of GI and HPB Surgery, Aster Medcity, Cochin

cycle1.result: Complete TME 148 (94.26%), nearly complete 7 (4.46%); safe CRM 151 (96.18%); negative distal margin 155 (98.73%); mean nodal harvest 19.86 ± 9.28; composite surgical success 95.54%.

audits.other_findings: Audit of laparoscopic rectal resections compared with trial benchmarks (ALaCaRT and ACOSOG Z6051).
audits.citation: Veerankutty FH, Nair N, Chacko S, Sreekumar VI, Varma D, Kurumboor P. Oncological adequacy of laparoscopic rectal cancer resection: An audit in Indian perspective. J Minim Access Surg. 2020;16(3):251-255. doi:10.4103/jmas.jmas_272_18. PMID: 31793449.
